messages:
alex.support: Heads-up — NovumHealth's private deployment in eu-west started getting intermittent 502s + API auth errors right after we applied the DirectConnect route update at 08:12UTC. Customer says TLS handshake failures visible in their logs and very slow DNS resolution from within their VPC.

deploy-bot: route-update: direct-connect peer 10.200.0.0/16 advertised -> action: replace-route-table by infra.oncall at 2025-03-16T08:12:03Z

maria.network: @alex.support can you paste a traceroute and BGP table snapshot? do we see asymmetric routing or a missing return path? :eyes:

alex.support: quick traceroute from a private node to api.private.novum.example:
```
traceroute to api.private.novum.example (10.200.5.21), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.2 ms
 2  192.168.100.1  1.5 ms
 3  10.254.0.1  4.1 ms
 4  * * *
 5  203.0.113.45  42.9 ms
 6  198.51.100.12  43.3 ms

looks like replies are egressing out a different path (hops drop after 3).
```

maria.network: show ip bgp summary from our DX router?

carlos.eng: pasted small BGP snippet we pulled from the customer's router (anonymized):
```
BGP table version is 1423341, local router ID 10.254.0.1
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcvd MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ  State/PfxRcd
10.200.0.1      4 65001   12421   12420  1423341    0    0  Established  142
172.31.5.2      4 64512    2211    2209  1423310    0    0  Idle (admin)  0
Routes: 10.200.0.0/16 -> next-hop 10.254.0.254 (via VRF-redwood-dx)
```

sam.oncall: can we get a packet capture on the egress interface during a failure window? specifically want to see TLS ClientHello and ServerHello SNI and cert. also need to see DNS queries (udp 53) and whether they time out.

alex.support: got a tcpdump from the customer's node while hitting the API: showing TLS handshake timeout + server cert for hosted.redwood.com (not private cert). snippet:
```
09:22:11.123456 IP 10.200.5.21.54321 > 172.31.10.10.443: Flags [S], seq 12345
09:22:11.223412 IP 172.31.10.10.443 > 10.200.5.21.54321: Flags [S.], seq 54321 ack 12346
09:22:11.224000 TLS ClientHello SNI: api.private.novum.example
09:22:11.325000 TLS ServerHello -> cert CN=api.redwood-hosted.com
09:22:11.350000 TLS alert: certificate_unknown
```

alex.support: customer-visible effect: client fails TLS validation because cert CN mismatch, then retries which triggers backend auth errors and 502s. DNS slowness also seen: their DNS queries to 169.254.169.253 (customer-resolver) time out and fallback to our recursive via peering, but that path is intermittent.

maria.network: hypothesis: route-change pushed traffic into wrong VRF / public-hosted egress. SNI hitting hosted fleet certificate because egress NAT or route maps send that traffic to our public edge, not the private-proxy cluster. also if OCSP/CRL egress is blocked from customer VPC -> cert validation can time out and cause TLS failures.

carlos.eng: we checked our peering access-lists: there was a route-map applied during the DX update that prepends and sets next-hop to 198.51.100.12 for 10.200.0.0/16 in one direction but not the reverse. looks like asymmetry + incorrect next-hop.

customer-rep: customer confirmed they didn't change anything on their side. they also showed cloud FW logs where outbound connections to cert OCSP servers were DROPPED to 203.0.113.0/24 after the peering change.

sam.oncall: immediate mitigations:
- rollback the route-map change on the DX peer to restore previous next-hop (we should schedule this ASAP if safe)
- add temporary egress allowlist for OCSP/CRL endpoints we saw in logs so cert validation doesn't timeout (customer FW)
- add a specific static route on their VRF to force api.private.novum.example -> correct private-proxy IP (bypass public egress)

carlos.eng: config suggestions we tested in lab:
```
route-map DX-IN permit 10
 match ip address 10
 set ip next-hop 10.254.0.254
!
ip access-list extended ALLOW-OCSP
 permit tcp any host 198.51.100.200 eq 80
 permit tcp any host 198.51.100.201 eq 80
```

alex.support: repro steps for customer engineering (short):
1) curl -v --resolve api.private.novum.example:443:10.254.0.110 https://api.private.novum.example/health -> observe cert CN and SNI in verbose output
2) dig +time=2 +tries=1 @169.254.169.253 api.private.novum.example -> see timeouts
3) tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp port 443 or port 53' -w /tmp/peering-issue.pcap while reproducing

maria.network: tagging network eng to review BGP community/route-map behavior. also we'll verify that our egress NAT policy for private deployments wasn't accidentally pointing to the public front-door after the route change.

carlos.eng: root cause (current theory): asymmetric BGP/route-map change on DirectConnect peering caused traffic to route to our public edge in return path; that public edge presents hosted certs and/or goes through egress paths blocked by customer's firewall (OCSP) causing TLS validation failures and API auth errors.

sam.oncall: next steps / timeline:
- 08:45 UTC: rollback tentative route-map (if no impact) -> monitor
- 09:00 UTC: customer will temporarily allowlisted OCSP/CRL IPs -> fast cert validation
- 09:10 UTC: we push a static host route for api.private.novum.example on the DX VRF to force correct next-hop
- 09:20 UTC: confirm with customer and close or continue investigation if flapping

alex.support: customer team is standing by; they gave access to their FW logs and pcap. I'll upload artifacts to the escalation ticket. thanks everyone. :pray:
